_meta.citation: Macknick, Newmark, Heath & Hallett (2012), Operational water consumption and withdrawal factors for electricity generating technologies: a review of existing literature, Environ. Res. Lett. 7 045802 (NREL/TP-6A20-50900).
_meta.note: Withdrawal is water taken from a source; consumption is the portion evaporated and not returned. Both are median operational factors for recirculating (tower) cooling. Factors vary heavily by cooling system -- once-through withdrawal is one to two orders of magnitude higher -- so a single national figure per technology papers over a real spread. Coal has among the highest consumption; nuclear the highest withdrawal. Solar PV and wind use essentially no operational water (panel washing only).

solar.note: Utility-scale PV; no cooling loop, so withdrawal equals consumption (panel washing).
